newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary has 100,000 T of excess white sugar - SIA.
newsitem.headline: Hungary has 100,000 T of excess white sugar - SIA.

text.p: Hungarian sugar factories have produced about 570,000 tonnes of white sugar from the 1996 beet crop, over 100,000 tonnes more than domestic needs, their organisation, the Sugar Industry Association (SIA) said on Wednesday.
The excess sugar will either be exported -- with a loss for the factories -- or stored until the next crop, deputy director Karoly Sotner told Reuters.
"If the amount of money the factories lose on export is smaller than the costs of storage then the stocks will be exported, otherwise it will be stored," he said.

If the sugar gets exported, its most likely destination will be the Balkans or the former Soviet Union, as both Central Europe and the European Union have sufficient stocks to cover domestic needs, Sotner said.
He said that it costs Hungarian factories between 73 and 80 forints to produce a kg of white sugar, while they will be unlikely to get more than a net 60 forints per kg on exports.
Exports outside Europe are even more uneconomic and will be unlikely to be pursued by the Hungarian factories.
Hungary does not subsidise white sugar exports.
Sotner added he believed that most of the 100,000 tonnes of sugar is still in Hungary currently.
The factories only have a couple of months to make up their minds whether they will export the sugar, as they will draft production contracts in March, he said.
If the stocks stay in the country, then the factories will have to contract for less beet, he explained.
Hungary's domestic white sugar consumption is about 450,000 tonnes a year.
